paper.title: Exploration and Incentivizing Participation in Randomized Trials

unmapped: Objective is worst-case mean-squared error of estimating each arm's average score over the main stage, maximised over all scoring functions f: Omega->[0,1] (counterfactual estimation for RCTs)
Mechanism must satisfy Bayesian Individual Rationality (participation incentives) w.r.t. agents' time-invariant (stochastic) Bayesian beliefs with known finite-support prior
Agents do not observe history or assigned arm (information asymmetry); mechanism has commitment power
Outside option U_out known to the mechanism; utility structure known
Warm-up stage of T_0 <= T/2 rounds excluded from estimation target
settings.definition_quote: The outcome table $\rbr{\outcome_{a,t}\in\outcomes:\,a\in[n],\; t\in[T]}$ is fixed in advance ... We posit that this entire table is drawn from some distribution, which we henceforth call an adversary. ... \err\rbr{\mech\mid\adv} = \max_{f:\outcomes\to[0,1],\; a\in[n]} \E\sbr{(\,\estF(a) - \advF(a)\,)^2}

settings.name_in_paper: Incentivized RCT, heterogeneous agents (public and private types)
unmapped: Objective is worst-case MSE of estimating each arm's average score over the main stage, max over scoring functions
Mechanism must be Bayesian Individually Rational and Bayesian Incentive Compatible (truthful reporting of private types) w.r.t. agents' beliefs
Agent types (public observed, private reported) chosen by the adversary; agents believe types drawn i.i.d. from known D_type
Full-support assumption on outcome distributions under the prior
Learner knows the type set, the utility structure and the type distribution of the beliefs
settings.definition_quote: We denote agent's type as $\type = (\pubtype,\subtype)$, where $\pubtype\in\pubtypes$ is the public type, and $\subtype\in\subtypes$ is the private type. ... The adversary now specifies the agents' types, in addition to the outcomes.

settings.name_in_paper: Heterogeneous agents with estimated type frequencies
unmapped: Objective is worst-case MSE of estimating each arm's average score over the main stage
BIR and BIC constraints w.r.t. agents' Bayesian beliefs
Mechanism is given an estimate of the main-stage type frequencies F_type
Learner knows the type set, utility structure and estimated type frequencies
settings.definition_quote: The mechanism is initialized with estimated type frequencies $\typeFreqEst$: a distribution over types that estimates $\typeFreq(\cdot \mid \adv)$ for the (actual) adversary $\adv$.

algorithms.name: (eps, psi_bar)-greedy main stage with IPS estimator
TwoStageMech(T_0, sigma_opt, best-arm policy) with MLE state estimate and IPS

symbols.bench: state-aware benchmark bench(P): inf over BIR state-aware policies of max over states and arms of 1/sigma_a(psi)

conditions: U*_P > U_out (best arm strictly improves over outside option)

source.label: thm:mech-single
source.quote: Assume $\bestVal>\ValOut$. Suppose mechanism \mech uses \greedy{\eps}{\approxstate} policy in each round of the main stage, where $\eps = \tfrac{n}{2}/\bench(\prior)$, and estimator $\estFreq = \ips$ ... Then: (a) $\err\rbr{\mech\mid\adv} \leq \frac{2\cdot \bench(\prior)}{T-T_0}$ for any adversary. (b) Suppose each arm appears in at least $N_{\prior}$ rounds of the warm-up stage ... Then the mechanism is BIR over the main stage.

results.notes: Quantity is worst-case MSE of counterfactual estimates (not regret). Part (b) (BIR given N_P = 32 alpha^-2 log(8n/alpha) warm-up samples per arm) is an incentive guarantee, not recorded as a separate bound.

conditions: mechanism is non-data-adaptive over a contiguous subset S of main-stage rounds with |S| >= c*T

source.label: thm:LB-single
source.quote: Fix prior $\prior$ and time horizon $T\geq \Omega\rbr{\bench(\prior)^{-2}}$ and $T_0\leq T/2$. Let $S$ be a contiguous subset of rounds in the main stage, with $|S|\geq c\cdot T$ for some absolute constant $c>0$. Fix mechanism \mech that is non-data-adaptive over $S$. Then some adversary $\adv$ has $\err\rbr{\mech\mid\adv} = \Omega\rbr{\frac{\bench(\prior)}{T}}$.

results.notes: BIR requirement of the mechanism is implied by the setting (used in proof).

symbols.bench: worst-case benchmark bench(P, Theta) over BIC, BIR state-aware policies (= max over types of per-type benchmark)

conditions: mechanism is non-data-adaptive over a contiguous subset S of main-stage rounds with |S| >= c*T

source.label: thm:worst-LB
source.quote: The statement in \cref{thm:LB-single} holds for benchmark $\worstbench$.

conditions: non-degeneracy condition (eq:worst-nondegen): best-arm policy strictly BIR and strictly BIC
tuning: sampling distribution = average of benchmark-optimal policy and best-arm policy at MLE state

source.label: thm:mech-hetero
source.quote: Assume \eqref{eq:worst-nondegen}. Let \mech be the mechanism $\mechname(T_0,\benchpolicy,\bestA[])$. Then: (a) $\err\rbr{\mech\mid\adv} \leq \frac{2\cdot \bench(\prior,\types)}{T-T_0}$ for any adversary. (b) Suppose ... each (arm, public type) pair appears in $\geq N_{\prior}$ rounds ... Then the mechanism is BIR and BIC over the main stage.

results.notes: Theorem 5.12 specifies the warm-up parameters (delta_P = eta*/8, N_P(eta*)); not a separate error bound.

symbols.delta_slack: additive suboptimality of the relaxed benchmark-optimizing policy

tuning: policy optimizing the benchmark up to additive delta
relaxed best-arm policy that is eta-BIR and eta-BIC with eta in (0, eta*]

source.label: thm:worst-UB-extension
source.quote: Assume \eqref{eq:worst-nondegen}. Let $\hatbenchpolicy$ be a state-aware policy which optimizes the $\inf$ in the benchmark \eqref{eq:worst-bench} up to an additive factor $\delta\geq 0$. Let $\hatpolicy$ be a state-aware policy which is $\eta$-BIR and $\eta$-BIC ... Then mechanism ... satisfies \err\rbr{\mech\mid\adv} \leq \frac{2\,\worstbench + 2\delta}{T-T_0}

symbols.F_diff: L1 distance between estimated and realized type frequencies

conditions: any adversary; F_type are its realized main-stage type frequencies
tuning: benchmark-optimizing policy computed for estimated frequencies

source.label: thm:hetero-UB
source.quote: Assume \eqref{eq:worst-nondegen}. Let $\typeFreqEst$ be some distribution over types. Consider mechanism $\mechname(T_0,\benchpolicy,\bestA[])$ ... The performance guarantee is as follows: \err\rbr{\mech\mid\adv} \leq \frac{2\rbr{\bench(\prior,\typeFreq) + C_{\prior}(\typeFreq,\typeFreqEst) \cdot \norm{\typeFreqEst-\typeFreq}{1}}}{T-T_0}

conditions: mechanism is non-data-adaptive over a contiguous subset S of main-stage rounds with |S| >= c*T
adversary restricted to have main-stage type frequencies F_type

source.label: thm:worst-LB est
source.quote: Fix prior $\prior$ and time horizon $T\geq \Omega\rbr{\bench(\prior,\typeFreq)^{-2}}$ and $T_0\leq T/2$. Let $\typeFreq$ be some distribution over types such that $\typeFreq(\cdot)\in \tfrac{\Z}{T-T_0}$. ... Suppose mechanism \mech is non-data-adaptive over $S$. Then some adversary $\adv$ satisfies $\typeFreq(\cdot\mid\adv) = \typeFreq$ and $\err\rbr{\mech\mid\adv} = \Omega\rbr{\frac{\bench(\prior,\typeFreq)}{T}}$.
